finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Serverless Prisma -> connection exhaustion
File: src/lib/db.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: createPrismaClient() instantiates a PrismaClient at module load for production with no pooler or connection-limit handling and the code relies on per-process Prisma clients in serverless deployments. This yields one DB connection pool per Lambda/edge instance and will multiply connections under scale.
Impact: connection exhaustion and outages when many serverless instances spin up (real failures commonly appear at hundreds of concurrent function instances / ~100-500 DB connections depending on DB plan). 
Fix: use a pooled DB proxy (PgBouncer / RDS Proxy) and move to a single, reused client pattern across instances (or reduce pool size via connection string) and document it for production.

[DB-2] Fallback mocks silently hide DB failures
File: src/lib/db.ts (L90-L220)
Evidence: createFallbackHandler returns empty arrays or mock-created objects when _isPrismaConnected is false (fallback path for findMany/create/update/delete), so code path continues as if DB calls succeeded while returning fabricated data. 
Impact: silent data divergence and logical corruption across core flows (users see success even when writes never reached the DB), causing business-impacting inconsistencies immediately when the DB is transiently unavailable.
Fix: remove or disable mock fallback in production; throw or return explicit errors and surface DB connectivity failures to callers.

[DB-3] Unbounded full-table read on rooms
File: src/app/api/fetch_all_rooms/route.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: rooms = await db.room.findMany() is called without any where/limit/pagination and returns the full rooms table to an authenticated endpoint.
Impact: table scans and huge network payloads once rooms grows (noticeable degradation by tens of thousands of rows; catastrophic with concurrent requests), causing timeouts and DB CPU exhaustion under moderate concurrent traffic.
Fix: require and enforce pagination/limits, add server-side filters (owner/tenant), and restrict this endpoint to admin use.

[DB-4] Stripe webhooks & checkout lack idempotency/transaction safety
File: src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (L1-L220), src/app/api/checkout/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: webhook handlers and checkout create/update user and subscription state via separate find/update/upsert calls without recording processed event IDs or using transactional guards; checkout creates Stripe objects then updates DB in separate steps. 
Impact: duplicate or out-of-order webhook deliveries and concurrent webhook retries can flip subscription flags or leave Stripe and DB out of sync (financial flow inconsistency and user entitlement errors) at modest scale or during billing storms.
Fix: persist Stripe event IDs with a unique constraint and guard reprocessing, wrap related DB changes in transactions where possible, and make external-side effects idempotent (or reconcile via single upsert keyed by event id).

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-5] Missing index on Room.hostId (high-read filter)
File: prisma/schema.prisma (Room model) (L1-L60)
Evidence: code queries rooms by hostId (db.room.findMany({ where: { hostId } })) but schema has no @@index([hostId]) on Room.hostId.
Impact: host-scoped queries will cause full table scans as rooms grow (noticeable slowdowns at tens of thousands of rows), hurting the high-traffic "my rooms" path.
Fix: add an index (@@index([hostId])) on the Room model and run a migration.

[DB-6] create_room is not atomic against LiveKit
File: src/app/api/create_room/route.ts (L260-L420)
Evidence: the route calls roomService.createRoom() on LiveKit and then db.room.create() in the DB with no compensating rollback if the second step fails.
Impact: resource leakage and inconsistency between LiveKit and DB (or phantom rooms) under transient DB errors or race conditions, causing operational overhead and broken UX at moderate traffic.
Fix: perform DB reservation first or implement rollback/cleanup (delete LiveKit room on DB failure) and add retries/monitoring.

--- INFO ---

[DB-7] Duplicate Prisma client files present
File: src/lib/prisma.ts
Evidence: a separate src/lib/prisma.ts exists that also constructs a PrismaClient with different logging/caching behavior; not necessarily used by all routes.
Use: useful context — review imports across the codebase to avoid multiple client implementations creating duplicate pools or inconsistent settings in production.
